ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image is a schematic diagram of a plant cell, with a relatively thick cell wall/boundary in its external shape, and multiple green chloroplasts, a purple cell nucleus, and other structures inside. Slightly to the right of the center of the cell there is a very large pale white cavity, occupying most of the space inside the cell, and on the right side there is a labeling line pointing to this large cavity. Reasoning: The question asks about the organelle that is a “small cavity in the cytoplasm, surrounded by a single membrane, containing water, food, or metabolic waste.” According to the biological definition, this kind of membrane-surrounded storage cavity is a vacuole; in the plant cell diagram, the conspicuous large central cavity is the central vacuole. Therefore the answer is vacuole.
